correctness.rationale: The Rayleigh min over vectors perpendicular to ones proves lambda_2 concave in the nonnegative rate vector; symmetrization cannot decrease it. Vertex-edge transitivity leaves exactly two independent rate orbits. Explicit orthogonal Laplacian eigen-decomposition gives min((n+1)s,s+gt), with ns+ndt/2=B. Solving both affine branches proves each case including the beta=1 interval. Nonnegative averaging proves every beta<1 optimizer has zero base weights. Verified cycle and hypercube exact spectra and independent numerical direct diagonalizations. No finite computation is used to infer a universal assertion.

originality.rationale: Statement-to-statement comparison: Sun et al. 2006 sets up general FMMP and SDP/MVU dual but does not give the exact all-transitive-base cone threshold, universal strict-regime support conclusion or integer wheel/cube corollaries. Boyd 2006 supplies convexity and discrete-time examples with zero edge rates, not these continuous-time cone thresholds. Ghosh-Boyd 2006 considers selection of additional edges rather than continuous rate allocation. Kirkland-Pati cut-vertex extremizers are not applicable to cones of connected bases. Exact published mathematical research index semantic-query IDs recorded; failure to retrieve matching claims is not independently sufficient for novelty. Unindexed broader coverage is residual risk.
residual_risks: The 2002 Kirkland–Pati original full text could not be inspected, although its reported cut-vertex extremal theorem does not imply the cone claim.
A wider graph-spectral extremal treatment not indexed in the searched sources may contain an equivalent cone criterion; negative search is not proof of global novelty.
Only invariant optimal rates are classified for beta at least one; arbitrary asymmetric optimizers are not completely classified.

value.rationale: The analytic dimensionless ratio 2lambda2(H)/d yields a natural complete structural resource-allocation phase diagram on every cone over a vertex-and-edge-transitive base. Crucially it decides when every optimal network deletes all otherwise available base edges and exhibits a critical continuum of designs, with sharp transitions at wheel size six and hypercube dimension four. This resolves a motivated hub-vs-periphery tradeoff beyond computing a routine spectrum or an arbitrary small numerical example.
